life_summary: Marriner Wood Merrill was born on September 25, 1832, in Sackville, New Brunswick, Canada. He joined the Latter-day Saint Church in April 1852 and immigrated to Salt Lake City in 1853, becoming one of the pioneering settlers of Cache Valley, Utah. Merrill developed a reputation as a dedicated administrator and community builder, establishing deep roots in the Richmond, Utah area. Over the course of his life, he raised an exceptionally large family, eventually having forty-six children. Beyond his ecclesiastical responsibilities, he served his community in numerous civic capacities, including as postmaster of Richmond and as a member of the territorial legislature, embodying the ideal of the pioneering saint.
church_summary: Marriner W. Merrill served as bishop of Richmond for eighteen years beginning in July 1861. He was ordained to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on October 7, 1889, and served as first president of Logan Temple beginning in 1884. He was also a counselor in the Cache Stake presidency from 1879 onward. Despite facing legal prosecution for unlawful cohabitation in 1889, from which he was quickly released, he remained active in Church leadership. He was summoned twice by Congress during the Smoot investigation but declined to appear. By his 1935 family reunion, his descendants numbered 797. He died on February 6, 1906, in Richmond, Utah.
